sentences.text: The extinct animal belongs to the genus Eocoracias, which contains only one known species, Eocoracias brachyptera.
This genus is classified within the parent group Coracii.
A specimen of Eocoracias is notable for preserving non-iridescent structural coloration on its feathers, a feature previously unknown in fossil birds.
Scientists have recorded exactly two fossil occurrences of this unique animal.
Fossils of Eocoracias have been discovered at the Messel Pit in Germany.
The genus was described by Mayr and Mourer-Chauviré in 2000.
Eocoracias brachyptera lived approximately 47 million years ago during the Lutetian stage.
The genus existed between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago.
